lines: - Fix false positive `PhanUnreferencedPrivateClassConstant`/`PhanUnreferencedProtectedClassConstant` with `--dead-code-detection` for a private or protected constant declared in a trait and used from a class using the trait: uses of the class's copy now count as references to the trait's constant, as they already did for trait properties and methods. A trait constant that is really unused is now reported once, on the trait, instead of once on the trait and once more for every class using it ([#5619](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5619))

- Fix false positive `PhanReadOnlyPrivateProperty` (and the protected/public variants) with `--dead-code-detection` for a property that is only modified by `unset($this->prop['key'])`, `unset(self::$prop['key'])`, `unset($this->prop)`, or `$this->prop['key']++`/`--`: these are now tracked as write references, as `$this->prop['key'] = ...`, `$this->prop['key'] .= ...` and `$this->prop++` already were ([#5617](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5617))

- Emit `PhanInvalidWriteToTemporaryExpression` for `unset()` of a dimension or property of a constant, class constant, literal, `new` expression or other temporary expression (e.g. `unset(self::DEMO['key'])`, `unset((new Foo())->prop['key'])`), which is a compile error in PHP ([#5617](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5617))

+- Fix false positive `PhanTypeMismatchArgumentNullableInternal` and `PhanTypeMismatchArgumentInternal` for passing null to the parameters of internal functions and methods that PHP declares as nullable, such as `mb_strlen($s, null)`, `substr($s, 1, $length)` with a `?int` length, `date('Y', $timestamp)` with a `?int` timestamp, `array_splice($a, 1, null)`, `bcadd($a, $b, null)` or `Closure::bind($closure, null, null)`. About 490 parameters of 350 functions and methods were not nullable in the signature map. They now match the stubs of php-src for PHP 8.1-8.6, for every bundled extension. `internal/check_signature_map_against_reflection.php` reports these differences, `internal/update_signature_map_from_reflection.php` fixes them for the extensions of the running PHP, and the new `internal/update_signature_map_nullability_from_stubs.php` reads them from the stubs of php-src

- Updated parameter types for internal functions which were made nullable in PHP 8.0, allowing null to be passed to represent the behaviour when the parameter was omitted ([#5616](https://github.com/phan/phan/pull/5616)). With `--target-php-version 8.5`, `closedir()`, `readdir()` and `rewinddir()` also accept null again and no longer accept a `Directory` object, which PHP rejects with a TypeError

- Fix `PhanIncompatibleCompositionConstant` for the constants that a trait gets from the traits it uses, which were not checked: they are now checked against the constants of the class using the trait, of its other traits and (before PHP 8.5) of its parent class, as PHP does ("P and Outer define the same constant (C) in the composition of Ch"). Fix false positive `PhanIncompatibleCompositionConstant` for constants with the same value on different lines, such as `[1, 2]`, `null` or `1 + 1` in two traits: the values were compared with their line numbers. Phan now evaluates the values and compares them with `===`, as PHP does, so `1 + 1` and `2`, or `self::A` and `1` when `A` is 1, are compatible, and `[1, 2]` and `[1 => 2, 0 => 1]`, `1` and `1.0`, or an enum case and its backing value are not. `self` in the value of a constant of a trait is the class using the trait. An int value of a constant whose declared type accepts `float` and not `int` is a float, as in PHP (`const float C = 1;` is `1.0`). A value that accesses a constant through a trait (`T::X`, or `self::X` in a trait that uses other traits) is reported, because PHP throws an Error when it evaluates it. `X::class` is the name that PHP gives, resolved with the namespace and the `use` statements (the class does not have to exist), and the integer operators (`%`, `|`, `&`, `^`, `<<`, `>>` and `~`) are evaluated for integers. Values that Phan does not evaluate are not reported: global constants other than `null`, `true` and `false` (`namespace\true` is a constant of the namespace), magic constants other than `__LINE__`, the integer operators for operands that are not integers, operations that throw (such as `%` by zero), operators applied to a class name that Phan resolves through a `use` statement, `self` or `parent` (it may know the name with other letters in uppercase than PHP), a value with a class constant that the declared type converts to float (PHP converts it only if it replaced the class constant at compile time), the value of a constant inherited from the parent class if it depends on the class that `self` is (PHP evaluates it in the scope of the class or of the parent class, depending on whether it evaluated it before), large arrays of literals of which Phan keeps only some elements (`ast_trim_max_elements_per_level`, `ast_trim_max_total_elements`), values that would take Phan more than 3000 steps to evaluate (a constant is evaluated again for each reference to it), and some expressions, such as `?:` and `self::X[0]`. Fix false positive `PhanConstantTypeMismatchInheritance` for a constant declared as `iterable` that overrides a constant declared as `array|\Traversable` (e.g. `?iterable` and `array|\Traversable|null`), which PHP 8.3+ accepts ([#5661](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5661))

- Fix false positive `PhanTypeInvalidDimOffset` after a condition on a key of an array element, such as `if ($x['a']['b'])`, `$x['a']['b'] !== null` or `is_string($x['a']['b'])`: Phan narrowed `$x['a']` to an array shape with only the key `b`, so reading `$x['a']['c']` afterwards was reported, when `$x['a']` was `array`, `mixed`, untyped or a generic array such as `array<string,mixed>` or the elements of `$_FILES`. The keys of declared array shapes are still checked

Compares Phan's param/return types for functions/methods with the param/return types found in a local svn checkout of the XML sources of docs.php.net.
* - name: parameter names (used for named arguments)
* - by-ref: whether a parameter is passed by reference
* - optional: whether a parameter is optional or variadic
+ * - nullable: parameters that are nullable for Reflection (`?int`) and not in the map, so that Phan rejects a null that PHP accepts
* - missing: functions and methods that Reflection knows but the map does not
+     * @return bool whether Reflection's type is explicitly nullable. `mixed` is not: the map may deliberately be narrower.
+     * @param string $type a type of Phan's signature map
+     * @return bool whether the type accepts null (an empty type and `mixed` accept anything)
+        // Only the top level counts: `array<string,int|null>` does not accept null
+     * @param array<int|string,string> $entry the entry of Phan's signature map
+     * @return bool whether a parameter is nullable for Reflection and not in the map (compared by position)
+    public static function hasNullabilityDifference(array $entry, ReflectionFunctionAbstract $reflection): bool
* @return array<int|string,string> the signature of $reflection in the format of Phan's signature map
* Returns the type for a parameter that Phan's map types as $map_type and Reflection as $reflection_type:
* the map's type, unless PHP accepts values that it rejects. Then the types that PHP accepts are added,
* or Reflection's type is used if the two have nothing in common (e.g. `string` for an `int` parameter).
-     * Nullability is not changed: whether internal functions accept null is handled separately.
+     * If Reflection's type is nullable (`?int`, `string|array|null`), the result is made nullable as well.
public static function correctedParameterType(string $map_type, string $reflection_type, \Phan\CodeBase $code_base): string

+ * Run it with each PHP version in order (8.1, 8.2, ..., 8.6), with the stubs of the php-src branch of that version:
+ * the running PHP version selects the map that is checked and the file that is updated (the base map for 8.1, the delta for 8.2+).
+ * The stubs of a branch can be exported without checking it out:
+ *     git -C php-src archive origin/PHP-8.1 $(git -C php-src ls-tree -r --name-only origin/PHP-8.1 | grep '\.stub\.php$') | tar -x -C stubs81
